closure_challenge.name: Closure-challenge benchmark
closure_challenge.our_entry: Entry of record (round 5, 2026-08-07) scored 0.0566 overall through the benchmark's own unmodified harness across six pre-registered scoring calls (RANS-identity floor, round-1 periodic-hills correction, round-2 extended to ducts and NASA hump, round-3 test-blind decline-gate, round-4 Reynolds-invariant duct rescale, round-5 untrained QCR2000 forward solve on the ducts). Rank 1 of 7 scored locally against the LIVE public board fetched 2026-08-11T23:33Z, which carries six entries and a new leader (Yang, 0.0580); our own scoring is done at the frozen benchmark commit deb91557, which scores but does not rank. A local scoring, not an official placement. P(rank 1) = 50%: a case-level bootstrap over the eight scored cases puts the probability that this ordering survives a comparable set of cases at 50%, and an eight-case sample cannot pin that tighter than 0-97% at 95%. The previous figure - P(rank 1) = 68%, 2-100% at 95% - is STRUCK as of 2026-08-11: it was computed against a FOUR-entry board that no longer exists, and our margin over Yang more than halved with the change, 0.002878 to 0.001365. Best result on the public board on TWO of the eight test cases (alpha_05_4071_4048, alpha_05_4071_2024) against the live six-entry board, and both of those two are the organisers' own unmodified RANS field, which our decline gate passed through untouched; the credit there belongs to the baseline every entrant is handed for free, not to our model, anyone submitting it unchanged scores exactly the same, and so the count belonging to our own model is ZERO of eight. Our model is best on no single case. STRUCK 2026-08-11, kept here rather than deleted so the correction stays visible: this counter read four of the eight test cases until the board went from four entries to six and the two alpha_15 hills went to Tian, Buchanan, Hickel and Dwight. That figure was measured against the FOUR-entry board and is not a statement about the standings now. The overall is a mean and not a count of wins, so 0.0566 is still the lowest number on the board; this entry wins on consistency, not on peaks, and that is the honest description of it. Not yet submitted to the benchmark's steward. The lead is not statistically decided against any of the four entries nearest us: the 0.001365 margin over Yang sits against a per-case spread fifteen times larger (t = -0.19, four of eight cases won), so on a different set of eight cases the ordering could reverse, and the same is true of Reissmann (t = -0.50), Wu and Zhang (t = -0.95) and Tian, Buchanan, Hickel and Dwight (t = -1.03); the margins over Liu and Montoya do survive that test. The standing is three deletions wide - drop any one of alpha_15_13929_4048, alpha_15_13929_2024 or alpha_05_4071_4048 and the point rank falls to 2, 3 and 2. AR_1_Ret_360 and AR_3_Ret_360 are ties below the precision the board publishes to, and are not per-case wins. Source: campaign/PROBABILITY_OF_RANK_SIX_ENTRY_2026-08-11.md; the superseded four-entry computation is kept at campaign/PROBABILITY_OF_RANK_2026-08-10.md.
